title: Rice Bug (Alitangya or Atangya): Damage, Thresholds and Control
metaTitle: Rice Bug (Alitangya): How to Spot and Control It in Palay
metaDescription: The rice bug, or alitangya, sucks milky grains and leaves palay empty and spotted. Learn when to count it, and when a spray is really worth it.
excerpt: The rice bug, Leptocorisa oratorius, is the slender, foul smelling insect that Tagalog farmers call atangya. It sucks the grains of palay (rice still in the husk) while they are still milky, and a heavy attack leaves panicles full of empty, spotted grains. This guide shows how to tell it from the black bug, when to count it, and when a spray really pays.

blocks.text: What the rice bug looks like

Most [rice insects](/pests/rice-insects) attack the leaves, the stems or the roots. This one waits for the grain. Adults are long and thin, with long legs and long antennae, and their color is greenish brown. The nymphs, or young bugs, have green bodies that blend with the leaves, so many farmers miss them.

Eggs sit in small batches along the midrib of the leaf. They are oval, shiny and reddish brown. Pick up an adult and you will know it at once, because it gives off a strong, bad smell. Adults feed in the early morning and late afternoon. Under bright sun they hide in grassy areas. Shake a hill and the nymphs drop down the plant, while the adults fly off a little way.
Rice ear bug, atangya, tayangaw and alitangya

In English you will read about the rice bug, the rice ear bug, the rice earhead bug or the rice seed bug. Tagalog farmers call it atangya or alitangya, Ilocano farmers dangaw, and many farmers in Western Visayas and parts of Mindanao tiangaw. One source from Camarines Sur gives tayangaw, so treat that one as a local word. The general words for insects and bugs in Tagalog are kulisap and insekto, and our list of [farm words in Tagalog](/blog/farm-words-in-tagalog) has more. Our guide to [alitangya in English](/blog/alitangya-in-english) puts every name side by side.

Be careful with alitangya. Tagalog dictionaries, Wiktionary among them, give alitangya as the name of the rice black bug, the round, dark stink bug also called itim na atangya. Plain atangya means the rice bug. Because the names overlap, trust the shape of the insect more than the name. A slender, long legged bug on the panicle is the rice bug. A broad, oval black bug at the base of the hill is the [rice black bug](/pests/rice-black-bug).
Rice bug scientific name and life cycle

The rice bug's scientific name is Leptocorisa oratorius. A close relative, Leptocorisa acuta, does the same damage, and many guides treat the two as one pest. Both belong to the family Alydidae, the broad headed bugs, in the order Hemiptera, the true bugs that feed by sucking.

A female lays her eggs in rows of about 10 to 20 on the upper side of the leaves or on the panicle. They start yellowish, turn reddish brown and hatch in about a week. The green nymphs then feed for about 18 days before they grow wings, so one generation takes about a month. In one study each female laid 75 to 135 eggs. That is why two or three waves can follow one another when the fields around you flower at different times.
How rice bugs damage palay

Both nymphs and adults push their mouthparts into the developing grain and suck out its contents. They feed from just before flowering up to the soft dough stage, and every soft, milky grain is at risk. The nymphs do more damage than the adults. Before the grains form, the bugs feed on young shoots and leaves, but the serious damage comes at the milky stage. Rice bugs can sometimes cut yield by as much as 30 percent.
Signs of rice bug damage

items: Empty or unfilled grains, and small or shriveled ones
Deformed grains with brown or dark spots where the bugs fed
Panicles that stay erect in heavily infested fields, since light grains do not bend them
A bad smell in the raw and cooked rice, and straw that cattle refuse to eat

blocks.text: Nutrient deficiency and flower [thrips](/pests/thrips) can leave similar grains. So before you act, confirm the cause by finding the bugs, their eggs or their smell.
When rice bugs build up

The bug lives in every rice environment, but it is more common in rainfed and upland rice. Between crops it lives on wild grasses, then it moves into rice fields when the crop flowers. It is less active during the dry season. Watch your field closely when:

items: Woodlands, weedy areas or wild grasses along canals sit next to your field
Farms around you plant at different times, so flowering fields follow one another for weeks
The monsoon rains begin, or the weather stays warm with overcast skies and frequent drizzles
The rainy season is ending, since numbers rise at that time

blocks.text: How to count rice bugs and when to act

items.title: Start before flowering
items.text: Begin scouting just before the panicles come out and keep going until the hard dough stage, a window of about 30 days.

items.title: Walk the field early or late
items.text: Go out at dawn or toward evening, when the bugs sit on the panicles. Walk diagonally across the field and check 20 hills.

items.title: Count every nymph and adult
items.text: Adults often fly off before you reach the hill, so write down what you find with the date and the lot.

items.title: Compare with the threshold
items.text: Consider a spray only when the count passes a threshold in the table below. If it stays under, keep counting instead of spraying.

blocks.caption: Action thresholds for atangya
rows: More than 5 nymphs and adults per square meter
More than 10 nymphs and adults per square meter

Cultural and natural control of atangya

items: **Clean the surroundings.** Cut grassy weeds in the field, on the pilapil (levees) and along canals, where the bugs breed between crops.
**Plant together.** When the whole community plants at once, bugs cannot move from early fields to late ones.
**Keep the crop even.** Even land, fertilizer and water let the whole lot pass the milky stage together.
**Net them.** Sweep a net through the crop at dawn or toward evening while numbers are low.
**Bait them.** Rotting meat, fish or snails draw the bugs to one spot, where you can destroy them.
**Grow awned varieties where you can.** Awned varieties resist the bug.
**Protect natural enemies.** Small wasps such as Gryon nixoni and long horned grasshoppers kill the eggs, and spiders and lady beetles eat the nymphs and adults.

blocks.title: Spraying too much brings pests back
blocks.text: Careless insecticide use kills the wasps and spiders that hold pests down, and then the pests return in bigger numbers. The [brown planthopper](/pests/brown-planthopper) is the classic example in rice.
Chemical control: Alika, Karate and lambda cyhalothrin

Use a pesticide only when the count calls for it. If your counts pass the threshold, choose a product whose FPA registered label lists rice bug on rice. Read that label for the rate, the number of sprays and the pre harvest interval. Rice bugs feed until the grain hardens, close to harvest, so the pre harvest interval deserves extra care.

Two familiar examples come from Syngenta. The Karate insecticide (Karate 2.5 EC) contains lambda cyhalothrin, a pyrethroid in IRAC Group 3A. The Alika insecticide (Alika 247 ZC) mixes lambda cyhalothrin with thiamethoxam, a Group 4A neonicotinoid. Both are broad spectrum, so they can also kill spiders and other friendly insects. Our guide to the [insecticide for rice bug](/blog/insecticide-for-rice-bug) compares every active ingredient and when to spray, and our guides to [Alika, Virtako and Chess](/blog/rice-insecticides-alika-virtako-chess) and [Karate, Cymbush and Selecron](/blog/karate-cymbush-selecron-insecticides) cover the brands.

blocks.text: Rice bug questions farmers ask

items.q: What is the rice bug called in Tagalog?
items.a: Atangya or alitangya in Tagalog, dangaw in Ilocano, and tiangaw in many Visayan towns. One Camarines Sur source gives tayangaw. Tagalog dictionaries also use alitangya for the rice black bug, so look at the insect before you decide.

items.q: What is the scientific name of the rice bug?
items.a: Leptocorisa oratorius, with the related Leptocorisa acuta. It is a true bug of the family Alydidae, in the order Hemiptera.
From just before flowering to the soft dough stage, while the grains hold milky sap. That window lasts about 30 days.

items.q: Are rice bugs and rice black bugs the same?
items.a: No. The rice bug is slender and feeds on milky grains in the panicle. The rice black bug is a round, dark stink bug that sucks sap at the base of the plant and can cause deadhearts and bugburn.

items.q: Which insecticide works on rice bugs?
items.a: Lambda cyhalothrin is the active ingredient most Philippine labels name for it on rice, as in Karate, and Alika mixes it with thiamethoxam. Use only FPA registered products whose label names rice bug, and follow the label. Our guide to the insecticide for rice bug lists the rest.
